headline: Members reviewed overdose data, discussed a new fentanyl derivative, and considered revisions to the mission statement and housing and warming station plans.
summary: Partner groups gave updates, including United Way and the NH National Guard. Members reviewed opioid overdose data, discussed revisions to the Mission and Vision Statements, and received a housing services update. The minutes record no votes or formal decisions.
plain_text:
1 | P a g e  
 
City of Nashua 
Division of Public Health and Community Services 
 
Mayor’s Task Force on Substance Misuse Meeting 
 
Tuesday, 07/21/2026 
9:30 – 11 a.m. 
Facilitator: Bobbie Bagley, Director DPHCS        Location: City Hall Auditorium, 3rd Floor 
Minutes 
 Partner Updates  
United Way  
• The new Director of the Prevention Coalition has been hired.  
• Provided an update on the lockbox initiative.  
• Reported that approximately 85% of individuals served are in recovery.  
• Announced the continuation of the Shoe Drive, accepting gently used shoes 
through the dedicated shoe fund.  
NH National Guard  
• Reported that summer activities have slowed.  
• A second staff member has been hired.  
• The D.A.R.E. Program has begun.  
• Participating in community trailer events and embedding staff within partner 
agencies.  
• Working with Public Health and United Way to strengthen partnerships.  
• Interested in expanding collaboration and job-shadowing opportunities.  
• Brief update provided on the Drug Nexus initiative.  
AMR Data 
• Slide presentation on AMR Data with information on opioid overdoses and 
opioid-related deaths.  
o Two overdose fatalities occurred during the previous week.  
o Two overdose deaths have occurred this month.  
o Members discussed the emergence of a new fentanyl derivative and 
concerns regarding a newly identified substance.  
• Year-to-date June data:  
o 16 overdoses  
o 2 overdose fatalities 
Mission, Vision and 
Goals Review 
The current Mission and Vision Statements were reviewed and read aloud.  
• A suggestion was made to include "Greater Nashua" in the Mission Statement 
to better reflect the coalition's service area.  
• Members discussed whether the wording of the statements should be revised 
to strengthen their overall impact and clarity.  
• An update was provided regarding the upcoming SAMHSA State Work Plan 
meeting.  
• Members noted that the priorities and approach for Greater Nashua may
2 | P a g e  
 
differ from those of Manchester.  
Suggested Revisions 
• Include language emphasizing continued innovation.  
• Add language focused on reducing stigma. 
Housing Services 
Update 
• Public Health does not proactively search for encampments but follows up 
when reports are received.  
• A GIS system is used to help locate and identify encampment locations.  
• It was reported that individuals have moved from several encampment 
locations, including: Behind Pheasant Lane Mall, Broad Street, Hudson Bridge, 
Celina Avenue  
• Members discussed the ongoing challenges related to accessing affordable 
and stable housing.  
• The Warming Station is scheduled to open on November 15 at Elm Street 
Middle School. •  Volunteers are needed to support Warming Station 
operations. It was noted that the available space is not ideal but will be used 
to provide shelter during the winter season. 
• Resource Center update was given.  
 
   
Next Meeting August 18, 2026
